question: The phenomenon of change of a liquid into vapour at any temperature below its boiling point is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**evaporation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Evaporation** is defined as the phenomenon of change of a **liquid** into **vapour** at any **temperature** below its **boiling point**. ***Hence, option B is correct.***
 
• **Solidification** is a phase transition in which a **liquid** turns into a **solid** when its temperature is lowered below its **freezing point**. ***Hence, option A is incorrect.***
 
• **Condensation** is the process by which **water vapour** (gas) in the air is changed into **liquid water**; it is the crucial process that forms **clouds**. ***Hence, option C is incorrect.***
 
• **Sublimation** is the transition of a substance directly from the **solid** state to the **gas** state without passing through the intermediate **liquid** phase. ***Hence, option D is incorrect.***
 
• **Evaporation** is a **surface phenomenon** where particles from the surface of the liquid gain enough **kinetic energy** to break away from the forces of attraction of other particles and escape into the air as vapour.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors Affecting Evaporation:**

 
 
• **Surface Area:** Since evaporation is a **surface phenomenon**, an increase in the **surface area** increases the rate of evaporation. For example, spreading out wet clothes to dry.
 
• **Temperature:** With an increase in **temperature**, more particles get enough **kinetic energy** to go into the vapour state, thereby increasing the rate.
 
• **Humidity:** It is the amount of **water vapour** present in the air. If the **humidity** is high, the rate of evaporation decreases because the air can only hold a certain amount of vapour.
 
• **Wind Speed:** An increase in **wind speed** leads to water vapour particles moving away with the wind, which increases the rate of evaporation.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Sublimation:** This process is observed in substances like **Naphthalene**, **Camphor**, **Ammonium Chloride**, and **Dry Ice** (Solid Carbon Dioxide). It occurs when the **vapour pressure** of the solid exceeds the surrounding atmospheric pressure.
 
• **Freezing Point and Solidification:** For **pure water**, the **freezing point** is **0°C** or **273.15 Kelvin** at standard **atmospheric pressure**. During this process, **heat energy** is released into the surroundings.
 
• **Condensation in Nature:** It is responsible for the formation of **dew**, **fog**, and **mist**. It happens when the air temperature drops to its **dew point**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evaporation vs. Boiling:** While both involve a phase change from liquid to gas, **boiling** is a **bulk phenomenon** that occurs throughout the liquid at a **fixed temperature** (e.g., **100°C** for water), whereas **evaporation** occurs only at the **surface** and at **all temperatures**.
 
• **Cooling Effect:** Evaporation causes **cooling**. This is because the liquid particles absorb **latent heat of vaporization** from the surroundings to change into vapour, leaving the surroundings cooler.
 
• **Practical Examples:** We use **cotton clothes** in **summer** because cotton is a good absorber of **sweat**, which then evaporates and provides a cooling effect. Similarly, water kept in **earthen pots** (matkas) stays cool due to evaporation through small **pores**.
 
• **Latent Heat:** During the change of state from liquid to gas, the **temperature** remains constant because the heat supplied is used as **latent heat** to overcome the **intermolecular forces**.
